readmeExcerpt:
# GitNexus

GitNexus indexes a codebase into a knowledge graph of symbols, calls, dependencies and execution flows. Use it through your coding agent's MCP tools, the CLI, or a web graph explorer. [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Documentation](#documentation) · [Web UI](https://gitnexus.vercel.app) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/MgJrmsqr62) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/172685ba-8e54-4ea7-9ad1-e31a3398da72 ## Quick start Requires **Node.js 22.18+ on 22.x, or 24.11+**. See [platform requirements](gitnexus/README.md#requirements) for Linux and Windows native dependencies. ```bash # Run from your repository root npx gitnexus analyze # Connect your editors once npx gitnexus setup ``` `analyze` builds the index, installs agent skills, registers Claude Code hooks, and writes `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` context files. `setup` configures MCP for your editors. Use `gitnexus analyze --index-only` to index without those repository integration files. For repeated use, install globally with `npm install -g gitnexus`. If installation fails, see [troubleshooting](gitnexus/README.md#troubleshooting). ## What you can do | Task | Tool | | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | | Find code and related execution flows | `query` | | Inspect a symbol's callers and dependencies | `context` | | Check what a change could affect | `impact` | | Trace a path between two symbols | `trace` | | Review the impact of a Git diff | `detect_changes` | | Preview and apply a semantic rename | `rename` | Ask your agent questions such as “What calls this function?” or “What would this change affect?” Resolution depends on language support and available evidence; check reported ambiguity, index freshness and coverage limits. ## Editor setup `gitnexus setup` detects Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Antigravity, Factory Droid, OpenCode, CodeBuddy and Qoder. Windsurf requires manual MCP configuration. To select editors: ```bash gitnexus setup -c cursor,codex ``` See [editor setup](docs/editor-setup.md) for the support matrix, manual MCP configuration, hooks and plugin installation. ## Everyday commands ```bash gitnexus analyze # Refresh the current repository's index gitnexus analyze --watch # Reindex as local files change gitnexus query "authentication" # Search the graph gitnexus impact UserService --direction upstream gitnexus status # Check index freshness gitnexus list # List indexed repositories gitnexus serve # Serve indexed repositories to the web UI ``` For multiple concurrent agents, use one `gitnexus mcp --http --port 3111` server and connect clients to `http://127.0.0.1:3111/mcp`. See the [shared-server instructions](docs/cli-reference.md#multi-client-setups-use---http-not-stdio). ## Web UI Run `gitnexus serve`, then open [gitnexus.vercel.app](https://gitnexus.vercel.app). The UI connects to the backend to browse indexed repositories and use AI chat. It uses the existing index; no re-upload or re-index is needed. For Docker, hosted deployments, image verification, or a local frontend, see [deployment](docs/deployment.md). ## Supported languages C, C++, C#, COBOL, Dart, Go, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, Objective-C, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Swift, TypeScript, Vue and Zig have registered providers. Support varies by construct; see the [language inventories](docs/languages/README.md) for measured behavior, exclusions and remaining gaps. ## Documentation | Read | For | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [CLI reference](docs/cli-reference.md) | Commands, indexing flags, watch mode, configuration and shared stores | | [Environment variables](docs/cli-reference.md#environment-variables) · [vector tuning](docs/cli-reference.md#vector-cutoff-tuning) | Runtime settings and search tuning | | [MCP reference](docs/mcp-reference.md) | All tools, resources, examples, policies and response budgets | | [Editor setup](docs/editor-setup.md) | Supported integrations and manual configuration | | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | Docker, Render, image signatures and local frontend setup | | [Wiki generation](docs/wiki-generation.md) | Model configuration and generated repository documentation | | [Runbook](RUNBOOK.md) | Index recovery, embeddings and operational troubleshooting | | [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) · [type resolution](type-resolution-system.md) | How the indexer and resolution layers work | | [Type-resolution roadmap](type-resolution-roadmap.md) | Planned work and acceptance criteria | ## Security and privacy The CLI indexes code locally without an LLM. Optional remote embeddings, wiki generation and AI chat use the providers you configure. The web UI accesses the backend it connects to. Review [security guidance](SECURITY.md) and [deployment authentication](docs/deployment.md#deploy-to-render) before exposing an index to other users. ## Development See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for setup and pull requests, [TESTING.md](TESTING.md) for validation, and [GUARDRAILS.md](GUARDRAILS.md) for repository rules. ## Enterprise GitNexus is available as an **enterprise offering** — fully managed **SaaS** or **self-hosted** deployment. Commercial use of the OSS version is also available with proper licensing. Enterprise includes: - **PR Review** — automated blast radius analysis on pull requests - **Auto-updating Code Wiki** — always up-to-date documentation (Code Wiki is also available in OSS) - **Auto-reindexing** — knowledge graph stays fresh automatically - **Multi-repo support** — unified graph across repositories - **OCaml support** — additional language coverage - **Priority feature/language support** — request new languages or features **Upcoming:** auto regression forensics · end-to-end test generation 👉 Learn more at [akonlabs.com](https://akonlabs.com) — for commercial licensing or enterprise inquiries, ping us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/AAsRVT6fGb) or email founders@akonlabs.com ## Community Integrations Built by the community — not officially maintained, but worth checking out. | Project | Author | Description | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [pi-gitnexus](https://github.com/tintinweb/pi-gitnexus) | [@tintinweb](https://github.com/tintinweb) | GitNexus plugin for [pi](https://pi.dev) — `pi install npm:pi-gitnexus` | | [gitnexus-stable-ops](https://github.com/ShunsukeHayashi/gitnexus-stable-ops) | [@ShunsukeHayashi](https://github.com/ShunsukeHayashi) | Stable ops & deployment workflows (Miyabi ecosystem) | | [KiloCode MCP workflow](Documentation/kilo-code-mcp.md) | [@oktanishq](https://github.com/oktanishq) | Guide to connect GitNexus MCP to Kilo Code and verify tools. | > Have a project built on GitNexus? Open a PR to add it here! ## License [PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](LICENSE). Commercial licensing is available through [akonlabs.com](https://akonlabs.com). ## Acknowledgments - [Tree-sitter](https://tree-sitter.github.io/) — AST parsing - [LadybugDB](https://ladybugdb.com/) — embedded graph database with vector support (formerly KuzuDB) - [Sigma.js](https://www.sigmajs.org/) — WebGL graph rendering - [transformers.js](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers.js) — browser ML - [Graphology](https://graphology.github.io/) — graph data structures - [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) — Model Context Protocol

readmeHtml:
GitNexus

GitNexus indexes a codebase into a knowledge graph of symbols, calls, dependencies and execution flows. Use it through your coding agent's MCP tools, the CLI, or a web graph explorer.

Quick start · Documentation · Web UI · Discord

Gitnexus_CLI.1.mp4

Quick start

Requires Node.js 22.18+ on 22.x, or 24.11+. See platform requirements for Linux and Windows native dependencies.

# Run from your repository root
npx gitnexus analyze

# Connect your editors once
npx gitnexus setup

analyze builds the index, installs agent skills, registers Claude Code hooks, and writes AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md context files. setup configures MCP for your editors. Use gitnexus analyze --index-only to index without those repository integration files.

For repeated use, install globally with npm install -g gitnexus. If installation fails, see troubleshooting.

What you can do

Task Tool
Find code and related execution flows query
Inspect a symbol's callers and dependencies context
Check what a change could affect impact
Trace a path between two symbols trace
Review the impact of a Git diff detect_changes
Preview and apply a semantic rename rename

Ask your agent questions such as “What calls this function?” or “What would this change affect?” Resolution depends on language support and available evidence; check reported ambiguity, index freshness and coverage limits.

Editor setup

gitnexus setup detects Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Antigravity, Factory Droid, OpenCode, CodeBuddy and Qoder. Windsurf requires manual MCP configuration. To select editors:

gitnexus setup -c cursor,codex

See editor setup for the support matrix, manual MCP configuration, hooks and plugin installation.

Everyday commands

gitnexus analyze                 # Refresh the current repository's index
gitnexus analyze --watch         # Reindex as local files change
gitnexus query "authentication"  # Search the graph
gitnexus impact UserService --direction upstream
gitnexus status                  # Check index freshness
gitnexus list                    # List indexed repositories
gitnexus serve                   # Serve indexed repositories to the web UI

For multiple concurrent agents, use one gitnexus mcp --http --port 3111 server and connect clients to http://127.0.0.1:3111/mcp. See the shared-server instructions.

Web UI

Run gitnexus serve, then open gitnexus.vercel.app. The UI connects to the backend to browse indexed repositories and use AI chat. It uses the existing index; no re-upload or re-index is needed.

For Docker, hosted deployments, image verification, or a local frontend, see deployment.

Supported languages

C, C++, C#, COBOL, Dart, Go, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, Objective-C, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Swift, TypeScript, Vue and Zig have registered providers. Support varies by construct; see the language inventories for measured behavior, exclusions and remaining gaps.

Documentation

Read For
CLI reference Commands, indexing flags, watch mode, configuration and shared stores
Environment variables · vector tuning Runtime settings and search tuning
MCP reference All tools, resources, examples, policies and response budgets
Editor setup Supported integrations and manual configuration
Deployment Docker, Render, image signatures and local frontend setup
Wiki generation Model configuration and generated repository documentation
Runbook Index recovery, embeddings and operational troubleshooting
Architecture · type resolution How the indexer and resolution layers work
Type-resolution roadmap Planned work and acceptance criteria

Security and privacy

The CLI indexes code locally without an LLM. Optional remote embeddings, wiki generation and AI chat use the providers you configure. The web UI accesses the backend it connects to. Review security guidance and deployment authentication before exposing an index to other users.

Development

See CONTRIBUTING.md for setup and pull requests, TESTING.md for validation, and GUARDRAILS.md for repository rules.

Enterprise

GitNexus is available as an enterprise offering — fully managed SaaS or self-hosted deployment. Commercial use of the OSS version is also available with proper licensing.

Enterprise includes:

  • PR Review — automated blast radius analysis on pull requests
  • Auto-updating Code Wiki — always up-to-date documentation (Code Wiki is also available in OSS)
  • Auto-reindexing — knowledge graph stays fresh automatically
  • Multi-repo support — unified graph across repositories
  • OCaml support — additional language coverage
  • Priority feature/language support — request new languages or features

Upcoming: auto regression forensics · end-to-end test generation

👉 Learn more at akonlabs.com — for commercial licensing or enterprise inquiries, ping us on Discord or email founders@akonlabs.com

Community Integrations

Built by the community — not officially maintained, but worth checking out.

gitnexus-stable-ops @ShunsukeHayashi Stable ops & deployment workflows (Miyabi ecosystem)
KiloCode MCP workflow @oktanishq Guide to connect GitNexus MCP to Kilo Code and verify tools.

Have a project built on GitNexus? Open a PR to add it here!

License

PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Commercial licensing is available through akonlabs.com.

Acknowledgments

  • Tree-sitter — AST parsing
  • LadybugDB — embedded graph database with vector support (formerly KuzuDB)
  • Sigma.js — WebGL graph rendering
  • transformers.js — browser ML
  • Graphology — graph data structures
  • MCP — Model Context Protocol

aiSummary.oneLiner: Codebase knowledge graph preventing AI coding assistants from missing dependencies or shipping blind edits.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: GitNexus analyzes source code to build a precomputed relational knowledge graph that explicitly maps architecture, dependencies, and call chains. It exposes this structural intelligence to AI coding assistants like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), providing them with a deep architectural view of the codebase. Instead of relying on language models to iteratively explore raw graphs, GitNexus precomputes clusters, traces, and impact scores at index time, delivering comprehensive context in a single tool call. This prevents breaking changes caused by AI agents lacking awareness of downstream dependencies and allows even smaller models to make safe, context-aware code edits.
keyFeatures: Precomputed relational intelligence: Pre-structures codebase graphs to prevent AI agents from missing context during code modification.
Comprehensive MCP toolset: Exposes 19 specific tools for agents to query impact radius, trace paths, and validate API shapes.
Dual operating modes: Offers both a fast local CLI for daily development and a browser-based Web UI for quick graph exploration.
Impact radius analysis: Identifies exactly which files and functions will be affected by a proposed change before it is applied.
Single-command setup: Indexes the repository, connects editors, and generates context files seamlessly using one CLI command.

useCases.title: Agent-assisted development
useCases.description: Equip coding assistants with deep architectural context to safely edit core services without inadvertently breaking downstream dependencies.

useCases.title: Blast radius analysis
useCases.description: Determine the full impact of changing a critical data structure or API route before writing any actual code modifications.

useCases.title: Codebase onboarding
useCases.description: Utilize the browser-based Web UI to visually explore and query the architecture of an unfamiliar or complex legacy repository.

useCases.title: API contract validation
useCases.description: Validate API response shapes automatically against consumer property accesses using the provided shape checking MCP tools.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers and AI practitioners relying on coding agents like Cursor or Claude Code to modify complex codebases. Particularly useful for teams working in large, highly interdependent repositories where blind AI edits pose significant risks.
